rationale: Zero-ask-approver regression check of 27294e84 against the two named targets, plus a sweep of the rest of the diff in this lens's territory. (1) S-STAGE PLUMBING SYNC vs the spec: FAITHFUL. The spec pins the sync commit's BEHAVIOR, not its porcelain mechanism — its Background describes 'the pathspec-scoped .beads sync commit' as the existing shape, and the surviving contract points are R4.2's artifact-confinement spirit and bead 6's fixture (vii) (artifact changes only in the sync commit). Building D by plumbing as C's tree plus the refreshed artifact blob makes the C->D delta artifact-only BY CONSTRUCTION — confinement equal to or stronger than the pathspec-scoped porcelain commit it replaces — and no AC anywhere pins the porcelain path. The two-ref transaction {C->D, marker->D} keeps the marker==tip invariant through the stage, which is what lets fixture (ix) (kill after sync) close the residual window I flagged as info in round 4 (R1-4-1): the re-run now resumes at the merge stage instead of stale-blocking after a stale-marker delete. That info item is thereby resolved beyond what I asked. (2) G-STAGE ROUTING INTO --resolve-merge vs the 127-consumed-not-modified non-goal: FAITHFUL, with one wording nit. The non-goal bars MODIFYING spec 127's shipped surfaces (adopt, preflight, --resolve-merge); the G stage does the opposite of a bypass — a preserved-merge conflict leaves marker==tip and the re-run resumes INTO the existing --resolve-merge machinery ('never around it'), with fixture (x) pinning convergence through the 127 machinery without re-panel or laundering. The preserved-merge semantics (forward reconcile, never abort) are untouched; what the reconcile completion path gains is only the clearing of 128's OWN marker ref — bookkeeping for new 128 state adjacent to the 127 surface, not a change to its recovery semantics. The plan's phrase 'reconcile path untouched' should strictly read 'reconcile SEMANTICS untouched; it additionally clears the 128 marker' — recorded as a trivial wording note, not a fidelity breach. REST OF THE DIFF: the corrected M-before-marker ordering strengthens fail-closedness (the commit object exists before any ref moves; a wholesale transaction abort leaves nothing advanced, marker included), preserving AC-6's tip-unchanged-on-refusal assertion; marker != tip now PROVES a foreign commit under the transactional invariant, so AC-7(i)'s stale-SHA behavior is preserved verbatim (fixture (xi) pins it) and the cannot-launder boundary is stronger than round 4's; the O_EXCL sweep lands both framings consistently with my round-4 R1-4-3 note (journal contributes the read-modify-write shape only). Nothing in the diff touches the standing verified core — trigger-2 discharge, the (c)-only vacations, dead option-2 arms, the 16-AC bead mapping, and the OQ resolutions all stand as verified across rounds 1-4. No asks; APPROVE.
